title: Tactical Game & Theme Integration
description: Connecting the SOS tactical game module and the multi-sector theme switcher across the site interface.
content: Successfully integrated the SOS/Tic-Tac-Toe verification subsystem with the global theme switching engine. This ensures that all interactive modules dynamically recalibrate their visual schemas across the 7 core chakra sectors (Crown, Throat, Root, etc.). Optimized the layout signaling to maintain sub-second response times when switching between high-fidelity tactical themes.

title: Responsive Pagination Engine
description: Refactored the core library pagination layout to improve mobile responsiveness using CSS Flexbox.
content:
Transitioning from inline static layouts to flexible CSS grids/flex layouts is always a relief. I ripped out the JavaScript `style.margin` inline injections for the library component today. It instantly felt cleaner in the DOM tree.

Mobile users will now see the pagination wrap elegantly instead of breaking the terminal container bounds. A small change, but vital for maintaining the immersive experience on small viewports.

title: Local AI Intelligence Integration
description: Integrated Ollama with Qwen2.5 and DeepSeek-Coder for local interface development.
content: Successfully installed Ollama and initialized local models: Qwen2.5:7b (4.7 GB) and DeepSeek-coder:6.7b (3.8 GB). Integrated these local intelligence endpoints with VS Code for sub-second inference targets. Qwen2.5 is performing optimally, while DeepSeek-coder is requiring further conflict resolution for full tactical sync.

title: Cursor IDE Install & Agent Prompting Benchmark
description: Installed Cursor and ran side-by-side prompting experiments against VS Code workflows and Antigravity agents.
content:
Completed a clean install of Cursor IDE and spent the session stress-testing how prompting behaves compared to my usual VS Code setup and Antigravity-style agent flows.

VS Code still feels like the baseline editor: extensions and manual context assembly win on predictability. Cursor pulls the model into the file tree and diffs in a tighter loop—less tab-hopping, more "show me the change" energy. Antigravity agents sit in a different lane: broader autonomy, higher variance, and a heavier hand on long-horizon tasks; Cursor felt more surgical when I wanted a scoped patch with immediate review.

Takeaway: keep VS Code muscle memory for shallow edits, reach for Cursor when I want chat + apply across the repo, and treat Antigravity-class agents as expeditionary units—not the same contract as inline assistant prompting.

title: Vitruvian Man // Anatomical Map & Field Journal Bridge
description: Shipped the interactive Vitruvian diagram on About, then pressure-tested how classical proportion maps to real routines—and why this journal exists.
content:
Locked in the full Vitruvian Man stack on the About page: SVG geometry (square, circumscribed circle, measurement rails), hover telemetry for proportional callouts, the seven-node chakra overlay tied to the same spinal axis, and the expandable chakra grid scan. Theme sync now drives stroke and gradient stops so the figure breathes with the same accent as the rest of the Time Machine UI.

Vitruvius was not decorating; he was arguing that beauty is commensurability—parts that agree with each other and with the whole. Translating that into real life means treating the week like a module system: a repeatable head-length for deep work, fixed margins for recovery, and a single "navel" checkpoint where I ask whether effort still lines up with the larger square I claim I am building.

This Field Journal is the plaintext audit trail for that habit. If the anatomical map is the idealized schematic, these entries are the field readings—what shipped, what snapped under load, and what proportion I need to recalibrate next.

title: Unity Boot Camp — 2D Micro-Prototype With AI Co-Pilot
description: First Unity 6.4 install and a guided 2D mini-game tutorial, accelerated by iterative AI prompting when I hit editor friction.
content:
Ran through a fresh Unity Editor install and onboarding pass—Unity Hub, Unity 6.4 as the supported baseline for this experiment, 2D template, and the baseline project hygiene checks (input system choice, build target sanity, version control ignore rules). Locking to 6.4 kept tutorial notes and package defaults aligned with current editor behavior.

Primary objective was a compact 2D prototype: player movement, a simple collectible or hazard loop, and one win/lose condition—enough to prove the pipeline without opening a full production scope.

Whenever the tutorial skipped a step or the inspector layout shifted between versions, I leaned on AI-assisted prompts to decode errors, suggest component wiring, and sanity-check C# snippets before pasting them in. The model was strongest as a glossary and debugger; it was weaker when I needed exact menu paths, so I cross-checked those against official docs.

Net result: a playable micro-build and a mental map of where Unity wants you to live (Scenes, Prefabs, Physics2D) versus where the friction hides (packages, serialization warnings, import defaults).

title: Opencode & Codellama Install — Agentic CLI Evaluation
description: Installed opencode CLI and Codellama for agentic development workflow comparison.
content:
Spin up opencode and Codellama today as complementary agents in the local toolkit. 

Opencode positioned itself as an interactive CLI assistant—think of it as the anti-Cursor: instead of the model seeing your files and diffs in a tight loop inside a VS Code-derived shell, opencode runs as a standalone terminal tool that pulls file context via glob/regex and presents the change back to you in Markdown before you approve it. The UX is more git-add than git-commit, if that makes sense. It reads your codebase via its own search tools, surfaces findings, and waits for your go-ahead before touching anything.

Codellama came up after the opencode session. Pulled the 7B model at 3.8 GB and set it as a quick-consult endpoint separate from Ollama's Qwen/DeepSeek cluster. It's lighter than the others and hits faster—useful as a disposable thinking partner when you don't want the full 7B+ context reloaded into GPU VRAM.

The contrast: opencode is a workflow agent (it does things), Codellama is a thinking agent (you ask, it answers). Both are local and privacy-first. Will integrate opencode more fully into the daily workflow—the approval loop UX feels like it could replace manual file edits for routine refactors.

title: Site Updates Panel & Theme Persistence
description: Integrated a dynamic site updates panel in the top menu and refined the theme persistence logic.
content:
Added a new 'Updates' panel to the tactical top bar. The panel dynamically fetches recent site changes, keeping the dashboard clean while surfacing new developments without needing a full archive dive.

Simultaneously overhauled the theme engine logic: the 'Throat' theme is now enforced as the default baseline on fresh visits. However, the system leverages sessionStorage to smoothly persist any selected theme across page navigations during an active session, resetting only when you disconnect the terminal. Also rolled out custom tactical scrollbar styling for the updates panel to match the interface's military aesthetic.

title: Architectural Pivot Analysis — MEVN & Nuxt 3
description: Explored the theoretical roadmap for upgrading this vanilla portfolio into a robust MEVN stack leveraging Nuxt 3 and Serverless hosting.
content:
Conducted a deep-dive architectural review into transitioning this static portfolio into a dynamic Next-Gen application using Vue 3 and Node.js. The objective was assessing how to pivot without breaking the live deployment or losing the tactical aesthetic.

The findings were highly decisive: moving to a modern framework unlocks massive capability. An integrated Node.js (Express) backend linked to a database kills the need for static JSON files and third-party form handlers, enabling purely native data operations like a hidden 'Classified Admin Center' for drafting entries directly via GUI.

More critically, the analysis illuminated the ideal path for Vercel deployment. Standard separate Express servers struggle in a serverless ecosystem unless explicitly mapped. But migrating directly to Nuxt 3 (Vue's meta-framework) resolves this natively. Nuxt's embedded 'server/api' engine automatically complies with Vercel's Serverless constraints without requiring configuration tweaks, offering SSR speeds alongside our robust tactical UI.
